fatal_errors: The proposed heat-treatment/short-range-order comparison does not reconstruct the composition- and temperature-dependent single-crystal compression study.
Chemical short-range order is introduced as a primary cause without supporting evidence or a validated method showing that the proposed treatments change only short-range order.
The hypothesis omits the governing cryogenic inertial-dulling and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier mechanisms.
Annealing versus rapid quenching can also change vacancies, dislocation density, segregation, precipitation, and grain structure, so the experiment does not isolate short-range order.
No prior evidence is cited despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
explanation: The response recognizes local lattice distortion as a possible source of dislocation resistance, which weakly overlaps with the target's MSAD-controlled solid-solution strengthening. Otherwise, it proposes a different, unevidenced short-range-order hypothesis. It does not reproduce the equiatomic ternary-to-quinary FCC single-crystal system, [1̄23] compression, 9–1373 K temperature sweep, strain-rate jumps, TEM comparison, or DFT/MSAD analysis. It also misses the observed low-temperature phonon-drag/inertial crossover and elevated-temperature Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type solute pinning. The random-versus-ordered baseline and falsification rule are directionally testable, but the processing comparison is heavily confounded and diffraction alone may not quantify chemical short-range order adequately. The proposed restriction to five-or-more-component alloys further conflicts with the ternary and quaternary alloys central to the target.
